Retained bounded diagnostic path without the new numeric-session codec: An integral Decimal produced by a known arithmetic child may re-enter the bounded state while retaining Decimal promotion. The compiler's numeric-result provenance is required; an external Decimal literal/variable or fractional/out-of-range child is not silently admitted. A Decimal saved by BIND then reread as a variable does not inherit arithmetic certification. This is a finite bridge, not a general Python Decimal implementation or all-i64-source-spelling guarantee.

Retained bounded diagnostic path without the new numeric-session codec: A nonempty typed chain reuses the six existing arithmetic kernels, keeping a bounded integral accumulator and Decimal promotion state across operations. Multiplicative chains start Decimal promotion, then materialize one final RDF value; additive chains retain left-to-right order. Every division, including intermediate division, must have an exact integral quotient, and checked range failures remain fatal.

All local sparopt Rust/TOML, its retained upstream provenance and the current chain patch provenance belong to the same compiled input authority as parser/evaluator. The actual source inventory and real ggen mappings assign planner files to semantic_query_planner; changed/missing/added code fails existing binding. An upstream manifest is a baseline identity, not proof that current patches are upstream or behavior-qualified.

New chain variants are appended after all prior Expression variants. Existing expression discriminants and payload hash streams remain unchanged, preserving existing operand-order choices for the default planner.

Retained bounded diagnostic path without the new numeric-session codec: A multiplicative operation whose zero result requires a negative Decimal sign explicitly fails before its sign can be lost. The current fixed numeric carrier cannot faithfully preserve original Decimal negative zero; the refusal is an open capability gap, not a mathematical or original-source rejection.

Evaluate/adapt first, then every tail raw operand in order before numeric conversion or arithmetic. A raised first operand stops the tail, while a returned child error remains a value. Tail fatal failure can therefore precede an earlier divide-by-zero calculation. After fetching succeeds, numeric validation occurs per operation, not eagerly for all tail numeric values.

Chain normalization returns the whole node unchanged without normalizing children; loop-join fitness is false. These are conservative completeness arms only: the actual private source-sensitive route must bypass the entire optimizer, whose other passes can reorder, suppress or move evaluation.

Expression walking, used-variable/group checks and aggregate rewriting visit first and every tail operand in source order. Display/SSE preserve a distinct ordered chain and nested boundaries; formatting is diagnostic transport, not an execution rewrite.

The same planner copies chain first/tail operands and their shared operator tags recursively in both directions, preserving order and nesting. It never uses Add/Mul overloads or order_pair to lower a chain. Graph/aggregate/order conversions use this same transport; surviving legacy OrderBy shape does not enable typed OrderBy execution. The separately declared SourceOrderBy transport retains raw keys directly.

Planner variable collection visits chain first then every tail recursively, preserving source visitation order and complete variable membership. Chains are not statically treated as boolean constants.

Only the explicit hidden entry enabled by the nondefault rdflib760-nullable-internal feature constructs nonempty arithmetic chains. Existing parse_query, parse_query_rdflib760 and updates retain their previous binary arithmetic policy. The entry is a Rust item for private cross-crate receiving, not a public CLI /5 mode.

The existing single expression dispatcher compiles a source chain once, with one outer capture_sparql around that sequence. Nested source chains retain independent captures. A chain reaching the legacy expression compiler and manually empty chains are explicitly refused rather than replaced by a fake None closure or invented catch. Ordinary prepared-query optimization may eliminate a dead chain branch before compilation; this is not a blanket pre-planning chain rejection guarantee.

The real grammar retains ordered additive/multiplicative first-plus-tail sequences before binary lowering loses source boundaries. Parenthesized nonempty sequences remain nested; parentheses around a bare variable or literal remain transparent. No flattening of old binary nodes or source-string reconstruction is permitted.

The existing RDF-only type lattice reports ANY for both chain variants; it does not infer total numeric results, absence, returned-error identity or fatal behavior. No optimizer permission follows from this conservative type.

Private COUNT skips only raised NotBound, counts returned None/error cells, and propagates other raised SPARQL or fatal failures. DISTINCT first evaluates membership and, only if unseen, evaluates again for the update, storing the second returned value's identity. COUNT(*) and COUNT(DISTINCT *) retain complete tuple-domain identity.

Retained bounded diagnostic path without the new numeric-session codec: Legacy and typed arithmetic share add/subtract/multiply/divide/plus/minus kernels. The private typed subset accepts bounded integer operands, represents integer multiplication as Decimal, and accepts division only for exact integral quotients; zero division is a SPARQL error. The separately specified chain extension admits integral Decimal results only from certified arithmetic children. External Decimal/floating/date operands, fractional quotient rounding, unsupported datatypes, signed Decimal zero and range overflow explicitly fail as unqualified fatal cases. This is not complete Python numeric promotion or precision parity.

Typed expression context conversion uses Result at the real Dataset boundary. RDF externalization/internalization failures propagate; None/error cells are carried without RDF conversion. Consumer raw leaves for Variable, Literal and NamedNode retain the Dataset's internal representation and check cancellation, avoiding an extra ExpressionTerm round trip or lexical normalization. This does not qualify original parser normalization or redefine the Dataset's own term identity.

Typed arithmetic Expr boundaries catch only raised SPARQL errors into returned error cells, retaining error kind and object identity. Each newly raised runtime error receives a fresh identity. Dataset/cancellation and unqualified numeric cases remain fatal failures, not returned SPARQL objects or legacy None.

Raw variable absence raises a fresh NotBound error while raw present None and returned errors remain values. Only syntactic variable operands turn None into raised NotBound or re-raise the stored error unchanged; Expr child error values instead reach the operator's value validation. Local present None/error masks initial RDF.

One existing AST dispatch owns legacy and optional typed raw evaluators. Named nodes, literals, variables and six arithmetic operators have typed handling; the later nonempty source-chain extension is separately specified. Unqualified expression branches explicitly reject typed compilation. Existing RDF-only evaluation retains its boundary. SimpleEvaluator nullable_expressions defaults to false and has no public enablement or /5 profile.

The existing Extend consumes the typed raw evaluator, writes returned RDF/None cells, preserves its input row for returned or raised SPARQL errors, and propagates fatal evaluation/conversion failures. Only RDF expression values require Dataset internalization. Original forget/remember/thaw lifecycle is a separate qualification obligation.

Private FILTER keeps true EBV and rejects false/None/returned or raised SPARQL-error outcomes while propagating Dataset and cancellation failures. Fatal propagation for bare variables is an intentional Rust safety contract: original Python bare-variable _ebv catches all raised exceptions, so this difference is not described as blanket RDFLib parity.

In the private typed lane, Group consumes input and accumulator updates before output; input or accumulation failure aborts with no aggregate rows, without further input consumption or per-group recovery. Finalization failures may occur after earlier groups were emitted and are not covered by the zero-output claim. The retained legacy Group path uses lowered variable keys and intentionally merges absent/None. Explicit SourceAggregateV1 raw/AS keys and empty-group behavior have separate contracts in semantic-numeric.toml; neither path qualifies complete original initial-context lifecycle or all grouping plans.

GroupKeyCell preserves the exact old Option<T> hashing stream for RDF and absent grouping keys; added solution-cell tags must not perturb the existing RDF-only group's iteration/limit behavior. The legacy lane still constructs RDF-only keys, while private typed keys may carry returned-error identity. This does not define a stable SPARQL group order.

The private typed lane refuses unqualified LeftJoin, legacy OrderBy, Lateral and Service operators explicitly. Only the separately declared sealed SourceOrderBy node receives source ORDER capability; default/non-source compilers still refuse that node. Existing full-cell hash-left-join carrier controls do not establish typed operator, condition, fatal-error or context qualification. No refusal silently falls back to the legacy expression lane.

Private SAMPLE distinguishes Pending from Selected(None). A successfully returned None/error/RDF value is selected exactly and prevents later evaluations; only raised NotBound skips, while other raised SPARQL or fatal failures propagate. Finishing without a selected value emits a present None cell. DISTINCT does not change SAMPLE behavior.

Each private typed graph-pattern iterator stops after yielding its first failure; subsequent next calls neither read additional input nor yield later successful rows. Extend/FILTER cannot resume after a fatal. The adapter affects the private typed lane only and does not retroactively change legacy error-stream contracts.

binary64-conversion-budget-v1 admits integer coefficient or complete Decimal representation first. After admission, specials/zero and adjusted exponent>=309 or<=-325 avoid power expansion. The middle range checks original abs(exponent) against materialized-power budget before allocation; cancelling trailing decimal zeroes or switching to pow5 must not evade admission. Ratio work is bounded by admitted inputs/power and fixed binary64 shifts. Defaults remain4096; scalar conversion has no output text or integer string-limit phase, while actual query text output retains its budget.

For a valid and budget-admissible context, the separate Decimal(float) constructor boundary emits FloatOperation before exact value conversion. A trapped FloatOperation returns no value and precedes conversion's coefficient-resource failure; an untrapped call returns the exact value with only that signal and no precision/Emin/Emax rounding. Context validity and context-resource admission are checked first. Signals are per-call outcomes, not a mutable global Context or create_decimal_from_float rounding implementation.

Explicit binary64 conversion constructs an exact Decimal without arithmetic context, rounding, display/reparse or FloatOperation. Reduced powers of two determine coefficient/exponent; zero sign survives, integral inputs have exponent0, Infinity sign survives, and selected quiet NaN follows the reference positive quiet empty-payload repr result. Fixed binary64 temporaries have denominator exponent at most1074 and coefficient at most767 decimal digits before final representation-budget checks. It requests neither pow10 nor output formatting; mixed arithmetic and query consumption remain separate.

After full Decimal representation admission, signed zero/Infinity retain sign, quiet NaN retains conversion sign/class while losing decimal payload, and signaling NaN raises SignalingNaNConversion without Decimal flags. Finite conversion rounds the exact ratio once; overflow becomes signed Infinity, underflow signed zero. It takes no Decimal context and does not apply context precision or FloatOperation. No string parser determines converted bits.

Admitted actual BigInt cache converts by one exact positive-ratio nearest ties-even rounding and bit assembly, without using text as the numeric conversion intermediary or intermediate float rounding. Existing coefficient admission may use bounded digit-count text. A result beyond finite binary64 yields IntegerOverflow, independently of integer text limits/output/input-character budgets. Coefficient admission still occurs first; resources remain typed core faults.

Strict binary64 add/subtract/multiply/divide remain individual source steps. Divide checks both signed zero denominators before hardware division even for NaN/Infinity numerator; other normal overflow/underflow/NaN outcomes remain values. No FMA, reassociation, finite-only gate or Decimal signal is substituted. Locked target nearest-rounding/gradual-underflow assumptions and unqualified NaN hardware payload/sign are explicit.

Unary plus preserves the actual binary64 value/bits, including negative zero, and unary minus applies float sign negation. Decimal unary rounding/zero-sign policy is not imported. Selected finite/signed-zero controls do not qualify signaling-NaN host behavior.

Equal/Less/Greater relations compare Integer, Decimal and Binary64 numeric values exactly within admitted input budgets. Integer/Binary64 comparison uses the actual integer and binary significand; Decimal comparison uses sign, coefficient and exponent without context arithmetic rounding, exponent-sized powers or an intermediate rounded subtraction. Scale and signed zero do not become unequal numeric values. Representation equality and RDF ordering remain different owners.

Comparison returns both Result<bool,NumericFault> and every signal reached before that result. After existing context/input admission, Decimal/Binary64 equality records FloatOperation but ignores its trap; ordered relations may trap FloatOperation before exact conversion and NaN handling. Quiet Decimal NaN equality emits no InvalidOperation; signaling NaN equality and Decimal NaN ordering do. Pure Binary64 NaN does not acquire Decimal signals. A later conversion resource refusal retains already reached FloatOperation; no original Python resource-policy parity is claimed.

The same compiled source authority captures numeric Rust/manifest, retained source/license provenance, frozen-case adapter and public frozen fixture. The composed semantic_numeric owner depends on semantic_json, runtime depends on the numeric owner, and actual functions/tests map through real ggen inspection. Source-derived constants, current execution and engineering adoption remain different evidence.

Decimal syntax follows the pinned pure-Python constructor: Python strip precedes removal of all underscores, full input is consumed, Unicode decimal digits reuse semantic_json, and the reference Unicode case-insensitive Inf/NaN grammar is explicit. Scale, exponent and negative zero survive construction. C-backend constructor limits and process integer conversion settings are separate qualification boundaries.

Each Decimal add/subtract/multiply/divide/unary operation uses the explicit HALF_EVEN context and the single finish owner. Precision and Etiny apply in one rounding, including carry, scale, signed underflow zero and subnormal-to-normal rounding. Division preserves the preferred exponent and nonterminating results; no f64 intermediate, reassociation or final-only rounding substitutes for per-step behavior.

The existing duration consumer delegates Decimal arithmetic to semantic_numeric while retaining its legacy Dec representation, display, split12 and failure propagation. Month division rounds HALF_EVEN to28 significant digits before exact floor; zero-sign projection and10000-byte input policy remain explicit. This migration does not connect the core to nullable query arithmetic or replace DatasetSession ownership.

BigInt add/subtract/multiply/unary operations remain exact within explicit resource budgets. They do not acquire Decimal precision rounding or an implicit per-operation integer text limit. This primitive multiplication is not a claim that RDFLib multiplicative chains use integer arithmetic.

Fixed Decimal formatting introduces no new rounding, preserves fractional scale and negative zero, and prints a positive-exponent zero as0 or-0 without expansion. Infinity/NaN spelling preserves their state. Integer formatting retains arbitrary-precision digits. The legacy duration scientific/fixed display policy is a separate adapter and must not be replaced by this formatter.

Base-ten integer grammar is distinct from Decimal: underscores occur singly between digits, ASCII control whitespace U+001C through U+001F is refused, Unicode digits reuse the common table, and signs/underscores do not count toward the explicit text limit while leading zeros do. None or zero disables that text limit without disabling resource budgets.

Infinity sign and NaN sign/signaling/payload are retained. Signaling NaN precedes quiet NaN, left precedence is stable, and payload truncation follows context. Invalid operations, ordinary division by zero, Infinity/zero and finite/Infinity retain their distinct results and signals; specials are not narrowed to a finite-integer approximation.

Finite Decimal retains independent sign, BigUint coefficient and BigInt exponent; zero sign and coefficient trailing zeros are observable. Construction is exact without context rounding. Saved arithmetic results are passed as numeric values, never fixed-formatted and reparsed to recover state; this core transport is not an RDF per-cell cache implementation.

Input codepoints, coefficient size, output characters and materialized powers of ten have explicit budgets. Power-of-ten/output expansion is checked before requested expansion; huge underflow and distant addends use compact decisions. Arithmetic permits bounded two-input temporaries; check_digits uses a four-bits-per-digit precheck before exact text-length rejection, not an exact pre-allocation digit bound. Binary64 conversion has its own fixed finite temporary bound and then checks the resulting representation; the power-of-ten budget is not a power-of-five budget. Resource faults never become numeric traps or successful missing values.

Per-operation signals remain explicit and separate from numeric values. Untrapped outcomes preserve complete expected signal sets; configured traps return primary signal and no value. Complete trapped flags are a declared core contract, not observed C-backend parity. Invalid lexical input is mapped by context parse to InvalidOperation while resource failures remain resource failures. Exact explicit Binary64 conversion emits no signal; the separate constructor boundary emits FloatOperation before value conversion after context admission. Neither path supplies mixed arithmetic or persistent context flags.

Integer true division rounds the exact admitted ratio once using the existing ratio owner; no independent operand f64 conversion, decimal context or text intermediary. Check left then right coefficient budgets before rhs0; retain quotient sign for zero/subnormal, reject zero divisor and infinite integer quotient with distinct faults. Input/output-text and pow10 limits are not additional scalar limits; admitted binary shifts remain bounded by input plus binary64 format.

Exactly two Binary64 items follow pinned builtin sum default int0 start: preserve0.0+first, one Neumaier step and final nonzero finite correction guard. No FMA/reassociation, cross-row compensation state, Decimal context or arbitrary-family dispatch. Each consumer update restarts its own pair sum; signed zero and nonfinite handling follow this selected C branch.
